correctness.rationale: The Poisson splitting into both/only-first/only-second marked resets gives exact diagonal age mass \(c e^{-at}\) and off-diagonal density \(e\lambda e^{-e\min(s,t)-\lambda\max(s,t)}\). Independent Gaussian displacements conditional on ages yield exact positive-excursion integrals. Mills estimates identify the strict diagonal saddle \(t_*=x/\sqrt{2Da}\). A controlled off-diagonal boundary layer of size \(O(1)\) yields factor \(4e\lambda/c\); the diagonal/off-diagonal weights give atom \((c/a)^2\) and positive \(\operatorname{Exp}(c/2)\) gap. When \(c=0\), independent Poisson streams give a product of exact Laplace marginals and Gaussian \(\sqrt{x}\) age-difference fluctuations. The standalone checker passed 4633 exact rational/numerical assertions for rate identities, published spatial transform, covariance, scaled tail and age-gap Laplace transforms. Finite checks are separate from the limiting proof.

originality.rationale: The assessed finding concerns hidden last-reset ancestry conditional on a rare joint positive excursion, including a nontrivial atom-plus-exponential age-gap law and a sharp contrast with exclusive resetting. The foundational 2026 paper already derives the full spatial pair law, and classic Marshall-Olkin shock distributions supply unconditional ages; these are credited and not claimed. No explicitly dominating conditional marked-history result was identified in inspected primary material; priority remains best-knowledge and independent review is absent.
residual_risks: The published exact two-position density already dominates all unconditional spatial pair-tail probabilities; those are treated as supporting computations rather than a standalone novelty claim.

Only the 1967 Marshall-Olkin abstract was accessible, not its full text; it is used for acknowledged historical shock structure rather than a whole-paper noncoverage conclusion.

value.rationale: The conditional history is a physically motivated mechanism-level observable: large co-outliers can have nearly identical reset ages without coming from the same reset event. It yields the exact common-last-event probability \((c/a)^2\) and gap law with exponential rate \(c/2\), both different from unconditional shock statistics; exclusive resetting instead produces \(\sqrt{x}\)-scale Gaussian age mismatch. This distinguishes latent synchronization caused by rare joint excursions from literal common resets, despite zero linear covariance, and supplies a reproducible prediction for reset-event history measurements.
